title: Agents can create, change or delete files only inside their project's repository folder
outcome: Agents can create, change or delete files only inside their project's repository folder
acceptance: A Windows host test proves each of the criteria above, including a PowerShell script whose $home assignment fails before a recursive delete

An agent's shell command or file tool that creates, changes, moves or deletes a file outside its project's repository folder and worktrees is refused before it runs, the file survives, and the session and Greg see a refusal naming the path
Engram holds the rule as project policy: the allowed roots are the project's repository folder and its worktrees, and the policy names the tool-owned exceptions
Installing a build Greg approved passes only through an explicit exception that Engram records with its path and approval
Reads outside the repository stay allowed, and Engram, Cargo and TermAl tool writes to their own homes and caches still work
The same command inside the repository folder or one of its worktrees runs
disposal_reason: Greg explicitly redirected scope in Advisor session-6219 on 2026-09-26: TermAl will not block dangerous operations; the repository-only rules are already recorded in Beads and Engram. Stop the planned host enforcement work and focus on cleanup and refactoring. Instruction-level repository write restrictions remain in force.
